{{Short description|British astronomer and physical chemist}}
{{use dmy dates|date=May 2026}}
'''David Flower''' is a British [[astronomer]] and [[physical chemistry|physical chemist]], an [[emeritus professor]] in the [[Durham University Department of Physics]]. He was [[editor in chief]] of the ''[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]]'' (MNRAS) from 2012<ref name=mnras>
{{cite web
 | author = Keith Smith
 | title = New MNRAS Editor-in-Chief  
 | work = RAS News & Press
 | publisher = [[Royal Astronomical Society]]
 | date = 2 July 2012
 | url =http://www.ras.org.uk/news-and-press/219-news-2012/2139-new-mnras-editor-in-chief
 | accessdate =2012-08-07}}</ref><ref name=a&g>{{cite journal|title=New editor for 'Monthly Notices'|journal=[[Astronomy & Geophysics]]|date=1 October 2012|volume=53|issue=5|pages=5.39–5.39|doi=10.1111/j.1468-4004.2012.53539_5.x|doi-access=free}}</ref> to 2026.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tonkin |first1=Sam |title=Black hole expert to become next Editor-in-Chief of MNRAS |url=https://ras.ac.uk/news-and-press/news/black-hole-expert-become-next-editor-chief-mnras |publisher=[[Royal Astronomical Society]] |access-date=22 October 2026 |language=en |date=25 March 2026 |quote=will take over from Professor David Flower at the end of 2026}}</ref> He is a [[Royal Astronomical Society#Fellows|Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society]], and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts]].

Flower's research is on the physics and chemistry of the interstellar medium, including atomic and molecular collision physics and [[astrochemistry]]. He has authored a book entitled "''Molecular Collisions in the Interstellar Medium''" which was published in 2007 by [[Cambridge University Press]] of the United Kingdom. He has a long list of research published in peer review journals.<ref name=bio-pg>
